title: Inbound contract
content: Inbound applies to both requests and responses and performs lossless normalization only. It preserves every field, maps standard Chat semantics into canonical Chat, carries non-Chat semantics as extensions, and performs no filtering or semantic rewrite.

title: Chat Process contract
content: For Chat protocol content, Chat Process performs the standard semantic mapping. For content without Chat semantics, it normalizes into extensions without inventing special semantics. All Relay-mode payload rewrites occur here on both request and response paths.

title: Outbound contract
content: Outbound maps canonical Chat plus extensions to the target standard protocol. It does not own general payload rewriting. Only fields that cannot be represented compatibly may be filtered, and only through an explicit allowlist/denylist contract.

title: Provider Compat contract
content: Compat performs provider-private adjustments around the provider boundary after standard protocol projection. It must preserve registered business fields, must not become a second Chat Process or Outbound, and must not own routing, SSE, retry, health, or control-state reconstruction.

title: Full-attempt client commit barrier
content: Provider response frames are retained in a request-local full-attempt buffer until a protocol-valid terminal is reached. Failed attempts are discarded or handled by Error/reselection before any business frame is committed to the client.

title: Error status policy
content: Internal request-stage failures use 598, internal response-stage failures use 599, and network failures use 502. External provider or upstream failures keep the linked real status; the client-safe message projection may redact private detail but must not replace the real external status.
